cards.title: MG paid to non-eligible agents by vendor

narrative.headline: Desert Riders paid the most MG to non-eligible agents.
bullets: Total MG to non-eligible agents is SAR 125.6M; top-3 vendors ≈ 31% of the total.
Concentration suggests policy-leakage risk at a few partners.
Recommend reviewing eligibility controls and exception approvals.

cards.title: Attendance shortfalls (below required days) by vendor

narrative.headline: Attendance shortfalls are concentrated in a handful of vendors.
bullets: Rapid Wheels shows the most shortfalls; thousands still received MG.
Shortfalls correlate with higher exception usage.
Focus exception reviews and communication on the top 3 vendors.

cards.title: Top-5 vendors by share of total MG

narrative.headline: MG payouts are concentrated—top-5 vendors ≈ 57% of total.
bullets: Concentration raises the impact of any single-vendor policy issues.
Consider tiered controls for large partners.
Track concentration monthly as a key risk indicator.

cards.title: Non-eligible agents who received MG — totals & average per agent (by vendor)

narrative.headline: Non-eligible MG is material at several vendors.
bullets: Average MG per non-eligible DA exceeds SAR 400 at top vendors.
High averages likely reflect repeated exceptions.
Recommend targeted policy refresh and exception caps.

cards.title: Months with >30% spike/drop in MG payouts

narrative.headline: Two months show >30% swings in MG.
bullets: March spike linked to onboarding push; April correction follows.
Large swings deserve pre-approval tracking and root-cause notes.
Monitor vendor-level drivers in swing months.

narrative.headline: Swing months are driven by the same three vendors.
bullets: Concentration of drivers suggests targeted corrective action.
Add pre-spike vendor briefings when onboarding surges are planned.

cards.title: Final payout more than 20% over MG (outliers)

narrative.headline: We found multiple over-MG outliers (>20%).
bullets: Outliers cluster in a few vendors and months.
Review incentive stacking or manual overrides.
Introduce thresholds for auto-review.

cards.title: Repeated MG within first 30 days after joining

narrative.headline: Repeated early-tenure MG is present.
bullets: Do early exceptions correlate with long-term performance?
Consider a graduated MG policy for first 30 days.

narrative.headline: Rate anomalies are concentrated in top partners.
bullets: Outlier share is elevated versus network baseline.
Introduce rate sanity checks at assignment time.

cards.title: Agents tied to multiple vendors in the same month

narrative.headline: A subset of agents are linked to multiple vendors in a single month.
bullets: Investigate potential reassignment or duplicate contracting.
Align MG payment ownership for overlapping cases.

cards.title: Cities with unusual eligibility or MG payment rates

narrative.headline: Two cities show elevated MG payment rates vs. overall.
bullets: Patterns are consistent across several months.
Consider city-specific controls or thresholds.
